alg-importance-sampling:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a measure space. An **unnormalized target density** is a measurable function $\tilde p:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ with
$$Z_p:=\int_{\mathsf X}\tilde p\,d\mu\in(0,\infty).$$
The target probability measure is $\pi(dx)=\tilde p(x)\mu(dx)/Z_p$. A **proposal density** is a measurable $q:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ with $\int q\,d\mu=1$; write $Q(dx)=q(x)\mu(dx)$. The input integrand $f:\mathsf X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable, and the input sample $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ is IID with law $Q$, in the sense of [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]. The normalizing constant $Z_p$ is known for this algorithm.

**Admissible conditions for an unbiased estimate:** $n\ge1$, $q>0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on $\{x:f(x)\tilde p(x)\ne0\}$, and the random variable
$$Y:=\begin{cases}f(X_1)\tilde p(X_1)/(Z_pq(X_1)),&q(X_1)>0,\\0,&q(X_1)=0\end{cases}$$
is integrable under $Q$. The support condition makes the value on $q=0$ immaterial to the target integral.

**Well-defined weights:** The reciprocal map $r(s)=1/s$ for $s>0$ and $r(s)=0$ for $s\le0$ is Borel. Its composition with $q$, multiplied by the measurable inputs, makes the piecewise weight and weighted integrand measurable ([[thm-composition-with-borel-functions-preserves-measurability]], [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]).

**Procedure and output:** For each supplied draw $X_i$, set $Y_i=f(X_i)\tilde p(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i))$ when $q(X_i)>0$ and set $Y_i=0$ otherwise. Return
$$\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nY_i.$$
Separate variance and central limit claims require the corresponding weighted second-moment hypothesis.
thm-ordinary-importance-sampling-is-unbi:
## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $\tilde p\ge0$ and $q\ge0$ be measurable densities with $Z_p=\int\tilde p\,d\mu\in(0,\infty)$ and $\int q\,d\mu=1$, and set $\pi(dx)=\tilde p(x)\mu(dx)/Z_p$ and $Q(dx)=q(x)\mu(dx)$. Let $f:\mathsf X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $\int|f|\tilde p\,d\mu<\infty$. Suppose $q>0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on $\{f\tilde p\ne0\}$ and $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are IID with law $Q$. For the ordinary importance sampling estimator in [[alg-importance-sampling]],
$$\mathbb E_Q[\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}]=\int f\,d\pi.$$
thm-ordinary-importance-sampling-finite-:
## Statement

Use the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-ordinary-importance-sampling-is-unbiased]]. Define
$$Y_i:=\begin{cases}f(X_i)\tilde p(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i)),&q(X_i)>0,\\0,&q(X_i)=0\end{cases},\qquad \theta:=\int f\,d\pi,\qquad \sigma^2:=\operatorname{Var}_Q(Y_1).$$
If $\mathbb E_Q[Y_1^2]<\infty$, then $\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}$ has finite variance and
$$\operatorname{Var}_Q(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}})=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}=\frac1n\left(\frac1{Z_p^2}\int_{\{q>0\}}\frac{f(x)^2\tilde p(x)^2}{q(x)}\,d\mu(x)-\theta^2\right).$$
This conclusion is choice-free. If, in addition, AC holds, then
$$\sqrt n\bigl(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}-\theta\bigr)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2).$$
No finite variance or normal-limit claim is made when the weighted second moment is infinite.
alg-self-normalized-importance-sampling:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a measure space. The unnormalized target density is a measurable $\tilde p\ge0$ with $0<Z_p=\int\tilde p\,d\mu<\infty$ and target $\pi(dx)=\tilde p(x)\mu(dx)/Z_p$. Let $q\ge0$ be a measurable proposal probability density against $\mu$, let $Q(dx)=q(x)\mu(dx)$, and let $f$ be a measurable real-valued integrand. The input $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ is an IID sample from $Q$ in the sense of [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]], with $n\ge1$. For target interpretation require $q>0$ $\pi$-almost everywhere. Write
$$W_i:=\begin{cases}\tilde p(X_i)/q(X_i),&q(X_i)>0,\\0,&q(X_i)=0.\end{cases}$$
This is a nonnegative unnormalized importance weight; the value on $q=0$ is immaterial under $Q$ and under the stated target support condition.

The reciprocal map that is $1/s$ for $s>0$ and $0$ for $s\le0$ is Borel. Its composition with $q$, multiplied by $\tilde p$, makes $W_i$ measurable by [[thm-composition-with-borel-functions-preserves-measurability]] and [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]].

**Procedure and output:** Compute $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nW_i$. If $S_n=0$, return the status **no estimate: zero observed target weight**. If $S_n>0$, return
$$\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN}}:=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nW_if(X_i)}{S_n}.$$
For consistency require $\mathbb E_QW_1=Z_p\in(0,\infty)$ and $\mathbb E_Q[W_1|f(X_1)|]<\infty$. A ratio CLT and its Monte Carlo standard error require finite second moments of $W_1$ and $W_1f(X_1)$.
thm-self-normalized-importance-sampling-:
## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a measure space, $\tilde p\ge0$ a measurable target density with $Z_p=\int\tilde p\,d\mu\in(0,\infty)$, $\pi(dx)=\tilde p(x)\mu(dx)/Z_p$, and $q\ge0$ a measurable proposal probability density with $Q(dx)=q(x)\mu(dx)$. Assume $q>0$ $\pi$-almost everywhere. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID with law $Q$, put $W_i=\tilde p(X_i)/q(X_i)$ for $q(X_i)>0$ and $W_i=0$ otherwise, and let $f:\mathsf X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Suppose
$$\mathbb E_QW_1=Z_p\in(0,\infty),\qquad \mathbb E_Q[W_1|f(X_1)|]<\infty.$$
Then the self-normalized estimate in [[alg-self-normalized-importance-sampling]] satisfies
$$\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN},n}\longrightarrow\theta:=\int f\,d\pi\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
On a finite prefix where all observed weights vanish, the algorithm's no-estimate status is interpreted as the value $0$ for this convergence statement; almost surely that fallback is eventually unnecessary.

## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$, $\tilde p$, $Z_p$, $\pi$, $q$, $Q$, $f$, and $W_i$ satisfy the hypotheses and definitions of [[thm-self-normalized-importance-sampling-is-consistent-under-finite-moments]]. Assume also
$$\mathbb E_Q[W_1^2]<\infty,\qquad \mathbb E_Q[(W_1f(X_1))^2]<\infty,$$
and assume AC for the central limit conclusion. Set $\theta=\int f\,d\pi$ and
$$\tau^2:=\frac1{Z_p^2}\mathbb E_Q\!\left[W_1^2(f(X_1)-\theta)^2\right].$$
This is finite under the stated second moments. Then the estimate in [[alg-self-normalized-importance-sampling]] satisfies
$$\sqrt n\bigl(\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN},n}-\theta\bigr)\Rightarrow N(0,\tau^2).$$
Define its plug-in variance estimate, when $S_n=\sum_iW_i>0$, by
$$\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}_{\mathrm{MC}}(\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN},n}):=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nW_i^2(f(X_i)-\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN},n})^2}{S_n^2},$$
and set this quantity to $0$ if $S_n=0$. Then, without using AC,
$$n\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}_{\mathrm{MC}}(\hat\theta_{\mathrm{SN},n})\longrightarrow\tau^2\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
Define $\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\mathrm{MC},n}$ to be the nonnegative square root of this plug-in variance. Then $\sqrt n\,\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\mathrm{MC},n}\to\tau$ almost surely. No finite-sample unbiasedness assertion is made.
def-importance-weight-effective-sample-s:
## Definition

For the nonnegative importance weights $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ in [[alg-self-normalized-importance-sampling]], with $n\ge1$ and at least one positive weight, define the **weight-based effective sample size** by
$$\operatorname{ESS}_w:=\frac{(\sum_{i=1}^nw_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^nw_i^2}.$$
It is a diagnostic of observed weight imbalance. It depends only on the weights, not on the integrand, proposal regions that were never sampled, or target mass outside the observed sample. It does not certify support coverage, finite variance, accuracy, or convergence.
